title: Lower tail vanishing for bounded complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, and let $L\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ be bounded with
$H^q(L)=0$ for $q>-d_C-1$. Then $\Hom(C,L)=0$.

Here $X$ is a scheme, the coefficients are the condensed coefficient rings of
[sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], pulled back to $\Lambda_X$ as in
[sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]; $\Mod(\Lambda_X)$ is the module-object category
of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and $\Cons$ is the category of constructible
$\Lambda_X$-modules [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The integer $d_C\geq0$ is a chosen
uniform bound from [sk-lem-uniform-constructible-ext]:
$\Ext^r(C,N)=0$ for every constructible $N$ and every $r>d_C$.
Write $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ for the sheaves isomorphic to small filtered colimits
of constructible sheaves, and define $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ to be the full subcategory
of $D(\Mod(\Lambda_X))$ on objects whose cohomology sheaves all belong to
$\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. The derived category and cohomology are those of
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Bounded means that only finitely many
cohomology sheaves are nonzero; $C$ is placed in degree zero and
$\Hom(C,L)$ means morphisms in this ambient derived category, with the shift
and Ext conventions of [def-pc-ext].

proof.text: Fix $C$ and $d_C$. We prove the assertion for every such bounded $L$ by strong induction on the finite number $N(L)=\#\{q:H^q(L)\neq0\}$. If $N(L)=0$, choose a complex $M^\bullet$ representing $L$. The map $0\to M^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism, since it is an isomorphism on every cohomology object. Its image is invertible in the derived category by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so $L\cong0$ and every map $C\to L$ is zero.

source.place: opening induction sentence; the case L=0, with the acyclic case written out

proof.text: If $N(L)=1$, let $q$ be the unique degree with nonzero cohomology. By [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single], $L\cong H^q(L)[-q]$. The definition of $\Dic$ in the statement gives $H^q(L)\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. Since $H^q(L)\neq0$, the upper-vanishing hypothesis forces $q\leq-d_C-1$, hence $-q\geq d_C+1>d_C\geq0$. By the Ext convention [def-pc-ext], $\Hom(C,L)\cong\Ext^{-q}(C,H^q(L))$ in the ambient module derived category. The last group vanishes by [det-ind-heart-ii-vanishing], applied with $B=H^q(L)$ and Ext degree $-q$.

source.place: one-cohomology-sheaf case, from L isomorphic to H^q(L)[-q] through Ext vanishing

proof.text: Assume $N(L)\geq2$ and the induction hypothesis for every complex satisfying the stated hypotheses with fewer nonzero cohomology sheaves. Let $q_0=\min\{q:H^q(L)\neq0\}$. Apply [lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-triangle] with $E=L$ and $n=-q_0$. It gives the distinguished triangle $H^{q_0}(L)[-q_0]\to\tau_{\geq q_0}L\to\tau_{\geq q_0+1}L\to H^{q_0}(L)[-q_0+1]$. The good-truncation formula of [def-kun-truncations] says $H^i(\tau_{\geq a}L)=H^i(L)$ for $i\geq a$ and zero otherwise. Thus $L\to\tau_{\geq q_0}L$ is an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf and hence is invertible in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $A=H^{q_0}(L)[-q_0]$, $T=\tau_{\geq q_0}L$, $B=\tau_{\geq q_0+1}L$, and let $a:A\to T$, $b:T\to B$, $c:B\to A[1]$ be the displayed triangle maps. With $e:L\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ the preceding isomorphism, define $u=e^{-1}\circ a$ and $v=b\circ e$. The triple $(1_A,e,1_B)$ is an isomorphism from $(A\xrightarrow{u}L\xrightarrow{v}B\xrightarrow{c}A[1])$ to the displayed distinguished triangle: $e\circ u=a$, $b\circ e=v$, and the last square is the identity. Thus the triangle with middle term $L$ is distinguished by (TR1) of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. The zero sheaf is constructible, hence ind-constructible by its constant filtered presentation. The only possibly nonzero cohomology sheaf in $A$ is ind-constructible, so $A\in\Dic$ directly from the definition, and $B\in\Dic$ by [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums](2). The only cohomology of $A$ is $H^{q_0}(L)$ in degree $q_0$; the nonzero cohomology degrees of $B$ are exactly those of $L$ other than $q_0$. Both are bounded and retain the required upper vanishing. Therefore $N(A)=1<N(L)$ and $N(B)=N(L)-1<N(L)$, and induction gives $\Hom(C,A)=\Hom(C,B)=0$.

source.place: general case: choice of q_0, canonical triangle, and verification of the hypotheses on both outer terms

proof.text: Write $u:A\to L$ and $v:L\to B$ for the first two maps of the triangle in step 3. For any $f:C\to L$, the map $v\circ f$ lies in $\Hom(C,B)=0$. Part (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], with $W=C$, gives $g:C\to A$ such that $f=u\circ g$. Since $\Hom(C,A)=0$, one has $g=0$ and $f=0$. This proves the induction step and hence the assertion.
